To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a novel Secured Out-sourced Content Based Image retrieval solution which allows looking for encrypted images in a cloud in an efficient manner, and which does not affect the retrieval performance.
we propose a novel Secured Outsource Content Based Image Retriever that allows looking for similar encrypted images stored into the clouds in an homomorphically form.
we have proposed and implemented a novel SOCBIR solution which does not require to send the signature to a trusted third party.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a secured outsourcing of content based image retrieval, which is a very important topic for cloud computing.
the problem of content-based image retrieval (CBIR) in the cloud.
the design and implementation of an efficient, privacy preserving and secured image retrieval solution, based on a homomorphally encrypted signature extracted from a homomorphical encrypted image.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed SOCBCIR scheme provides a very efficient solution for content-based image retrieval from homomorphically Paillier-encrypted images, and that the proposed SOCRCBIR scheme provides a new way to conduct face recognition from homomorphical encrypted images.
the proposed solution is an efficient and secured SOCBIR scheme, which allows to look for encrypted images in a homomorphism way without requiring to communicate with a third party.

the SOCBIR proposed in this paper is the first one to our knowledge to propose an image retrieval system based on encrypted data, which does not need the cloud to communicate to a trusted third party, while keeping a similar image retrieval performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a novel way to compare encrypted images, which does not require the use of any trusted third party, and which is able to extract an encrypted global image signature from an encrypted image.

we propose a new way to compute a global image signature, which can be extracted in a homomorphic encrypted form, without requiring the cloud to communicate neither with a trusted third-party nor with the user, and without any extra-communication.
we present a novel solution that allows to look for similar medical or biometric images in a homomorphic encrypted form, without changing image retrieval performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a cloud provider is not able to know the image content and that the proposed SOCRIR is not affected by the cloud provider dishonest behavior, as usually the case in other existing schemes.
the SOCBIR is the only existing solution which allows retrieving encrypted content without the help of a trusted third party and which does not change image similarity retrieval performance.
the SOCBIR can be used in a wide range of applications where privacy is required.
